## Design

### 2026-11-04: I basically started working on the project by reading the guide very carefully first before doing anything and acually understanding stuff and taking in account even small stuff. so first i started of

**3.6h**

I basically started working on the project by reading the guide very carefully first before doing anything and acually understanding stuff and taking in account even small stuff. so first i started off by placing the rp2040 symbol then wired the 1.1v and 3.3v to it's pins on the mcu, then after that i placed down all the required decoupling capacitors specifically for 1.1v : 8  0.1uF capacitors  and 1 1uF capacitor so a total of 9 capacitors and for the 3.3v 2 0.1 uF capacitors and 1 1uF capacitor. After doing all that i moved on to the USB c where i had a little of a problem because in the guide the usb that was used had 2 pairs of d+ and d- (data lines) but the symbol i placed had only 1 d+ and 1 d- so i took my time to look thru each usb c symbol to make sure i didn't make any errors and sure enough i found out i was using the wrong symbol but after that i wired gnd, the data pins (wich i also later connected to the mcu)  and lastly the vbus (wich is the power that will go to the mcu) had to go thru an LDO so following the guide i placed it down and connected all itìs required pins. And to finish off this entry i placed the crystal oscilators global labels so "XIN" and "XOUT".
